claim: MoBA partitions the context into blocks and applies MoE-style top-k gating where the affinity score is the inner product between the query and the mean-pooled keys of each block, attending only to selected blocks with a causal constraint.
stance_target: The repo's description of CSA2's hierarchical/pooled-block indexer as scoring pooled block representations
scope_conditions: Context length N divided into n blocks of size B = N/n; score s_i = <q, mean pool(K[I_i])>; g_i = 1 iff s_i in top-k
quoted_support: the score si is computed by the inner product between q and the mean pooling of K[Ii] along the sequence dimension: si = <q, mean pool(K[Ii])>

claim: MoBA adds no parameters and removes none, making it a drop-in substitute for full attention, and sliding-window attention and attention sink are special cases of MoBA under particular gating networks.
stance_target: Whether block-sparse attention can be swapped into an existing architecture without changing the parameter count
scope_conditions: Same parameter count as full attention; hybrid full/sparse transitions supported
quoted_support: MoBA is designed to be a substitute for full attention, maintaining the same number of parameters without any addition or subtraction. ... both can be viewed as special cases of MoBA

claim: At 8K sequence length, MoBA and full attention track within 1e-3 LM loss across five models from 568M to 2.1B parameters (fitted curves 2.625*C^-0.063 vs 2.622*C^-0.063).
stance_target: Whether block-sparse attention matches dense attention at the training context the repo's baseline uses
scope_conditions: Five Chinchilla-optimal models: 568M/10.8B tokens, 822M/15.3B, 1.1B/20.6B, 1.5B/27.4B, 2.1B/36.9B; block size 512, top-k 3, sparsity up to 81.25%
quoted_support: the validation loss differences between these two attention mechanisms remain consistent within a range of 1e-3

claim: When the maximum sequence length is raised from 8K to 32K (95.31% sparsity), MoBA shows a marginally higher trailing-token LM loss than full attention in all five experiments (fitted 1.546*C^-0.108 vs 1.464*C^-0.097), with the gap narrowing as compute grows.
stance_target: The claim that CSA-style block sparsity pays off at 32k training context — at these scales it trails full attention on trailing-token loss
scope_conditions: Same five models trained at 8K then evaluated with max sequence length 32K; trailing LM loss over the last 2K tokens, counted only for sequences reaching max length
quoted_support: although MoBA exhibits a marginally higher last block LM loss compared to full attention in all five experiments, the loss gap is progressively narrowing

claim: A MoBA/full hybrid recipe — MoBA for 90% of tokens then full attention for the last 10% — reaches a loss nearly identical to full attention at 32K, with no significant loss spikes at the switch.
stance_target: Whether a 32k sparse-attention experiment can be made to match dense quality
scope_conditions: Three 1.5B models trained on 30B tokens at 32K context, block size 2048, top-k 3
quoted_support: the MoBA-only recipe results in higher position-wise losses for trailing tokens. Importantly, our MoBA/full hybrid recipe reaches a loss nearly identical to that of full attention.

claim: MoBA-only training gives higher position-wise losses for trailing tokens at 32K, so the sparse pattern must be paired with a full-attention tail rather than used alone.
stance_target: The claim that a pure sparse-attention run at 32k matches dense quality
scope_conditions: 1.5B model, 30B tokens, 32K context, block size 2048, top-k 3
quoted_support: the MoBA-only recipe results in higher position-wise losses for trailing tokens

claim: Block granularity matters: at 1.5B parameters and 32K context with sparsity held at 75%, there is a 1e-2 LM-loss difference between the coarsest setting (2 of 8 blocks) and finer settings (4/16, 8/32, 16/64, 32/128).
stance_target: Whether the block size choice materially changes sparse-attention quality at 32k
scope_conditions: 1.5B model, 32K context, 8/16/32/64/128 blocks with 2/4/8/16/32 selected, 75% sparsity
quoted_support: there is a performance difference of 1e-2 between the coarsest-grained setting (selecting 2 blocks from 8) and the settings with finer granularity. These findings suggest that fine-grained segmentation appears to be a general technique for enhancing the performance of models within the MoE family

claim: A layer-wise hybrid that switches the last several Transformer layers from MoBA to full attention significantly reduces SFT loss, motivated by MoBA being suboptimal during SFT because prompt tokens are masked out of the loss, creating a sparse-gradient problem.
stance_target: Whether a sparse-attention experiment on this box can survive the SFT stage
scope_conditions: SFT with loss masking on prompt tokens; number of hybrid full layers varied 1/3/5/10
quoted_support: we propose a hybrid approach — switching the last several Transformer layers from MoBA to full attention, while the remaining layers continue to employ MoBA. ... this strategy can significantly reduce SFT loss.

claim: Llama-8B-1M-MoBA matches Llama-8B-1M-Full within noise across 15 downstream benchmarks, including LongBench@32K at 0.4828 vs 0.4821.
stance_target: Whether block-sparse attention preserves downstream quality at long context
scope_conditions: Continual pre-training from Llama 3.1 8B Base, 128K -> 256K -> 512K -> 1M with position interpolation

claim: MoBA achieves up to 6.5x speedup when prefilling 1M tokens and a 16x reduction in attention computation time at 10M tokens.
stance_target: The magnitude of the sparse-attention win at very long context, which the run must scale down for 32k
scope_conditions: 1M model, sequence lengths 8K-1M; fixed sparsity ratio 95.31% (64 blocks, top-k 3) across 8K-10M
quoted_support: it achieves a speedup ratio of up to 6.5x when prefilling 1M tokens. ... at 10M tokens moba achieves a speedup ratio of 16x reduction in attention computation time

claim: MoBA's gate is learned end-to-end as part of the model, so adopting it requires training the block router — unlike HISA's training-free hierarchical indexer.
stance_target: Which of the two sparse-attention options the repo's CSA2 experiment should specify
scope_conditions: MoBA is a trained architecture with the same parameter count as full attention; HISA replaces the indexer at inference with no fine-tuning
quoted_support: MoBA is designed to be a substitute for full attention, maintaining the same number of parameters without any addition or subtraction. This feature inspires us to conduct smooth transitions between full attention and MoBA.
